subject: maths
chapter_title: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round

concepts.title: The Circle and Its Symmetries
concepts.definition: A circle is the set of all points at one fixed distance, the radius, from a centre; every diameter halves it, rotation about the centre maps the circle onto itself, and every chord has a matching reflection - making the circle the most symmetric of figures.
concepts.key_idea: One centre, one radius, endless symmetry: turn or fold, the circle covers itself.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh105.txt sections 5.1-5.2 (definitions, symmetries of a circle)
question_patterns: define a circle with its centre and radius
how many lines of symmetry does a circle have
explain the rotational symmetry of a circle
what is a chord and how is it different from a diameter
state the relation between radius and diameter
why is a circle called a symmetric figure

solution_steps.explain: All points equidistant from the centre form the circle.
Any diameter is a line of symmetry; the centre is the rotation point.
Chord, arc, sector and diameter follow from the same picture.

concepts.title: Equal Chords Subtend Equal Angles
concepts.definition: Chords of equal length cut off equal angles at the centre, and the converse holds too; measuring angles at the centre by the arcs they open gives the standard method of comparing chords.
concepts.key_idea: Same chord length, same central angle: the centre is the fair judge of chords.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh105.txt section 5.4 (chords and the angles they subtend)
question_patterns: show that equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre
two chords subtend equal angles at the centre - what can you say about the chords
prove the chord-angle theorem with congruent triangles
compare the two chords from the given central angles
state the converse of the equal chords theorem
apply the theorem to find the given angle

solution_steps.explain: Connect the centre to the endpoints of both chords.
Equal radii and equal chords give congruent triangles by SSS.
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles give equal central angles.

concepts.title: Perpendicular from the Centre to a Chord
concepts.definition: The perpendicular dropped from the centre on a chord always bisects the chord; the converse also holds - the line joining the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it - and both facts follow from congruent right triangles on either side.
concepts.key_idea: Centre to chord, straight and perpendicular: the chord splits into two equal halves.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh105.txt section 5.5 (midpoints and perpendicular bisectors of chords)
question_patterns: prove that the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord
a chord of length the given value is at the given distance from the centre - find the radius
state the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem
find the midpoint length of the chord from the given data
why is the line from the centre to the chord's midpoint perpendicular
apply the theorem to the given circle figure

solution_steps.explain: Draw the segment from the centre meeting the chord at right angles.
The two triangles on either side share a leg and hypotenuse equal to the radius.
RHS congruence gives equal halves of the chord.

concepts.title: Chord Length from Radius and Distance
concepts.definition: The perpendicular from the centre builds a right triangle with the radius as hypotenuse, so a chord at distance d from the centre has length 2 times the square root of (radius squared minus distance squared) - farther chords are shorter.
concepts.key_idea: Radius is the slant, distance the leg: half the chord completes the right triangle.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh105.txt section 5.6 (distance of chords from the centre)
question_patterns: find the length of a chord at distance 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 13 cm
a chord of the given length is at the given distance from the centre - verify
which of two chords is longer given their distances from the centre
find the distance of the chord from the centre
why do chords nearer the centre run longer
compute the half-chord using the Pythagorean relation

solution_steps.explain: Radius squared minus distance squared gives half-chord squared.
The square root is the half-chord; doubling gives the chord.

concepts.title: Angles in the Same Segment
concepts.definition: Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal, and the angle in a semicircle is a right angle; equal arcs give equal chords, so arcs, chords and angles order themselves consistently around the circle.
concepts.key_idea: One arc, many viewing points, one angle: the same-segment theorem in one line.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh105.txt section 5.7 (angles subtended by an arc)
question_patterns: prove that angles in the same segment are equal
show that the angle in a semicircle is a right angle
find the angle subtended by the given arc at the remaining circle
equal arcs of a circle subtend what kind of angles - justify
apply the same segment theorem to find the unknown angle
compare the angle at the centre and at the circumference for the same arc

solution_steps.explain: Choose the arc whose subtended angles are being compared.
The central angle doubles any angle at the circumference on the same arc.
Two angles viewing the same arc from the same segment must be equal.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the length of a chord at distance {d} cm from the centre of a circle of radius {r} cm.

extracted_variables.r: radius of the circle in cm
extracted_variables.d: distance of the chord from the centre in cm

solution_template.explain: r squared minus d squared gives half-chord squared.
Double the half-chord for the full length.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A circle of radius {r} cm has a chord {d} cm from the centre. How long is the chord?

extracted_variables.d: distance from the centre in cm

solution_template.explain: The full chord is twice the root.
